comparison_policy.rule: Never rank efficiency or power across records unless useful service, measurement planes, operating conditions, conversion stages and uncertainty method are matched. Source-reported values remain attributed to their source. A missing boundary remains unknown and blocks a superiority claim.

source.title: On the Efficiency Limits and Electric Field Stresses of Wireless Charging for Electric Buses: A 50-kW Experimental Study Based on Opportunity Charging
source.publisher: IEEE Journal of Emerging and Selected Topics in Power Electronics

service.application: 50 kW-class inductive opportunity charging for electric buses

measurements.name: prototype_power_class
measurements.measurement_plane: prototype rating / nominal class as stated in paper title
measurements.boundary: declared prototype power class; not independently interpreted as continuous average or receiver load power

measurements.name: dc_to_dc_efficiency
measurements.measurement_plane: DC-to-DC system boundary as reported by the study
measurements.boundary: DC-to-DC efficiency; not grid-input-to-battery or lifecycle efficiency
conditions: reported operating range includes up to 100 mm X/Y misalignment

measurements.name: stray_magnetic_field
measurements.measurement_plane: study-reported stray-field measurement location and method
measurements.boundary: stray magnetic field; not a complete exposure-compliance assessment
conditions: prototype operating condition from the study

known_unknowns: grid-side mains-to-receiver efficiency is not the reported DC-to-DC metric
full meter-plane and uncertainty detail must be taken from the primary paper before round-robin replication
long-duration field availability and lifecycle maintenance are not established by the reported efficiency result
the reported stray-field value alone does not establish exposure compliance for every installation

source.title: NTT and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Achieved World's Highest Efficiency in Laser Wireless Power Transmission under Atmospheric Turbulence

measurements.name: transmitted_optical_power
measurements.measurement_plane: transmitted optical beam output
measurements.boundary: optical power after laser generation; excludes electrical wall-plug input to the laser

measurements.name: receiver_electrical_power
measurements.measurement_plane: electrical output extracted from receiving panel
measurements.boundary: receiver electrical output

measurements.name: optical_to_electrical_efficiency
measurements.measurement_plane: receiver electrical output divided by transmitted optical power
measurements.boundary: optical-output-to-receiver-electrical; not wall-plug-to-load

measurements.name: continuous_delivery_duration
measurements.measurement_plane: demonstration operating interval
measurements.boundary: duration of continuous power delivery
conditions: laser and receiver system each installed inside safety booths

known_unknowns: electrical wall-plug input to the laser transmitter is not included in the 15% boundary
whole-system wall-plug-to-useful-load efficiency is not stated in the announcement
longer-term uptime, maintenance and availability are not established
the result is not directly rankable against an end-to-end electrical-input LPT efficiency without boundary normalization

source.title: DARPA program sets distance record for power beaming

measurements.name: receiver_delivered_power
measurements.measurement_plane: power delivered by the optical receiver as stated in public release
measurements.boundary: receiver-delivered power; complete source and receiver conversion planes not disclosed in announcement

measurements.name: transmission_duration
measurements.measurement_plane: reported transmission interval
measurements.boundary: duration of the >800 W delivery event

measurements.name: campaign_energy_transferred
measurements.measurement_plane: campaign aggregate energy transferred
measurements.boundary: aggregate campaign energy; not a single continuous delivery interval

known_unknowns: electrical input to the laser and complete wall-plug-to-receiver efficiency are not provided in the public release
receiver electrical measurement plane and conversion-stage losses require the technical report
30-second record does not establish continuous grid-like availability
the >1 MJ campaign total must not be interpreted as one uninterrupted service event

source.title: System-level design and experimental demonstration of a laser power transfer system

measurements.name: delivered_electrical_power
measurements.measurement_plane: photovoltaic receiver electrical output
measurements.boundary: reported useful receiver power
conditions: continuous operation under reported alignment and thermal conditions

measurements.name: end_to_end_lpt_efficiency
measurements.measurement_plane: overall LPT system boundary as described by the paper
measurements.boundary: reported end-to-end LPT efficiency; exact meter placements and inclusion of all auxiliaries require full-text extraction

measurements.name: laser_driver_electrical_efficiency
measurements.measurement_plane: electrical input and laser-driver output stage
measurements.boundary: laser-driver stage only; not complete LPT efficiency

known_unknowns: exact source and receiver meter plane definitions require full-text extraction before independent comparison
the 95.96% driver stage must not be substituted for the 12.4% whole-LPT result
uncertainty, repeatability and long-duration availability require the full paper and independent replication
the 12.4% end-to-end result is not directly rankable against NTT's optical-output-to-receiver-electrical 15% boundary

source.title: Simulation and Experiment of a Medium-Distance Underwater Ultrasonic Wireless Power Transfer System

service.application: underwater ultrasonic power delivery to a resistive load

measurements.name: transmitter_power
measurements.measurement_plane: transmitter power as reported in the paper abstract
measurements.boundary: exact distinction between wall supply and transducer electrical input requires full-text confirmation

measurements.name: received_load_power
measurements.measurement_plane: received power in 1.2 kΩ load
measurements.boundary: receiver load power

measurements.name: transmission_efficiency
measurements.measurement_plane: transmission efficiency as reported by the paper
measurements.boundary: source's stated UWPT efficiency; wall-plug-to-load boundary needs full-text verification

known_unknowns: wall-plug electrical input and exact transducer-side source meter plane require full-text confirmation
acoustic intensity distribution and propagation loss partition are not in the abstract
cavitation, biological exposure, marine fouling, reliability and field deployment remain separately unqualified
the source-reported 17% must not be ranked against optical or inductive efficiencies

source.title: A world first: dynamic wireless charging on a motorway

service.application: dynamic inductive charging on a 1.5 km A10 motorway pilot section

measurements.name: instantaneous_wireless_transfer_power
measurements.measurement_plane: wireless system transfer power as reported by project announcement; exact meter plane unspecified
measurements.boundary: instantaneous transfer power; not route-average energy or end-to-end efficiency

measurements.name: average_wireless_transfer_power
measurements.measurement_plane: wireless system transfer power as reported by project announcement; exact meter plane unspecified
measurements.boundary: average power under optimal steady-state conditions; averaging window and meter plane not stated in announcement

measurements.name: pilot_roadway_length
measurements.measurement_plane: instrumented pilot motorway segment length
measurements.boundary: roadway infrastructure length, not an energy-transfer distance for a single receiver

known_unknowns: whole-route source-to-battery efficiency is not reported in the announcement
power meter plane, averaging window, vehicle speed and per-vehicle energy are not stated
all-weather availability, traffic utilization and fleet-scale lifecycle economics are not established
optimal steady-state values are not a guaranteed continuous operating envelope

source.title: Laser-Based Far-Field Wireless Power Transfer for UAV Recharging: Architecture and Experimental Validation of the Pointing, Sensing, and Control System

service.application: UAV laser power-link pointing, sensing and photovoltaic receiver architecture; energy-delivery efficacy not fully measured
service.medium: free-space infrared optical link with hierarchical beam pointing

measurements.name: laser_electrical_to_optical_efficiency_parameter
measurements.measurement_plane: source model parameter: electrical laser input to emitted optical power
measurements.boundary: paper states eta_laser=0.30 for the current system; not presented as a complete end-to-end battery-delivery measurement
conditions: declared in the paper's system efficiency chain
does not include free-space interception, PV conversion or battery conditioning

measurements.name: pv_optical_to_electrical_efficiency_parameter
measurements.measurement_plane: photovoltaic receiver conversion parameter: incident optical power to cell electrical output
measurements.boundary: paper states eta_cells=0.20; downstream receiver electronics between cell output and battery input are explicitly neglected
conditions: representative receiver-chain parameter as stated by the authors
not an independently validated full battery-side efficiency

measurements.name: spot_center_and_diameter_calibration_error
measurements.measurement_plane: camera-based spot-center and diameter estimator against checkerboard metric reference
measurements.boundary: calibration estimator error; not receiver-pose uncertainty or energy-transfer efficiency
conditions: mean error below 2% in calibration campaign

measurements.name: outdoor_coarse_pointing_error
measurements.measurement_plane: difference between desired UAV target position and ground-station optical pointing result
measurements.boundary: coarse pointing error; not beam interception probability or delivered power

measurements.name: fine_steering_y_step_residual
measurements.measurement_plane: measured spot-center displacement versus nominal fine-steering mirror Y-axis steps
measurements.boundary: step-response residual; not dynamic tracking error under arbitrary flight disturbances
conditions: nominal 0–400 mm Y sweep in 50 mm steps

measurements.name: fine_steering_cross_axis_drift
measurements.measurement_plane: measured X-axis spot-center drift during a Y-only fine-steering sweep
measurements.boundary: cross-axis coupling in the tested scanner configuration

measurements.name: infrared_spot_diameter_fit_slope
measurements.measurement_plane: linear fit of measured infrared beam spot diameter versus propagation distance
measurements.boundary: empirical spot-diameter interpolation within tested range; not received-power or efficiency
conditions: spot measurements at long range including 100 m and 150 m

measurements.name: infrared_spot_diameter_fit_intercept
measurements.measurement_plane: intercept of measured infrared beam spot diameter versus distance fit
measurements.boundary: empirical spot-diameter interpolation within tested range; not received-power or efficiency

measurements.name: infrared_spot_diameter_fit_r_squared
measurements.measurement_plane: goodness-of-fit statistic for measured infrared spot diameter against distance
measurements.boundary: regression fit quality; not a physical transfer performance metric
conditions: linear spot-diameter fit over the paper's tested range

known_unknowns: No independently metered useful battery-terminal energy or end-to-end optical-to-battery efficiency is reported by the paper.
The 30% laser and 20% PV chain figures are source-declared architecture parameters and must not be multiplied or presented as a measured system efficiency.
The paper explicitly neglects the downstream electronic efficiency between photovoltaic cell output and battery input.
The outdoor coarse pointing error of 10–80 cm at approximately 15 m demonstrates unresolved calibration and actuation error, not qualified dynamic in-flight tracking.
The paper states that a full control-theoretic characterization of bandwidth, settling time and disturbance rejection was not part of the campaign.
The prototype-level controlled-access test posture is not a complete laser-safety certification or public-airspace deployment authorization.

source.title: Fault-tolerant multi-leg inverter-fed roadway-powered dynamic wireless power transfer charging system

service.application: quasi-dynamic roadway inductive charging with fault-tolerant multi-leg transmitter converter

measurements.name: design_power_rating
measurements.measurement_plane: system design target as stated by the article
measurements.boundary: declared 1000 W design; the article separately reports 800 W nominal experimental output
conditions: laboratory prototype with MATLAB and ANSYS analyses

measurements.name: nominal_aligned_receiver_output_power
measurements.measurement_plane: receiver-side DC output as reported for full coil alignment
measurements.boundary: reported receiver output power; exact source-input and calibration meter planes need full-text extraction

measurements.name: normal_operation_efficiency
measurements.measurement_plane: system efficiency as reported for normal operation
measurements.boundary: paper-reported efficiency; exact end-to-end meter planes and uncertainty are not specified in the public text extraction

measurements.name: coil_transition_low_output_power
measurements.measurement_plane: receiver-side output during transmitter-coil handover
measurements.boundary: transient low point during adjacent-coil transition; not average route power
conditions: brief transition dip reported for less than 80–120 ms

measurements.name: coil_transition_duration
measurements.measurement_plane: receiver output-power transient during pad-to-pad handover
measurements.boundary: duration of temporary power dip; not complete route-level interruption availability
conditions: dynamic receiver movement between adjacent transmitter coils

measurements.name: fault_isolation_low_output_power
measurements.measurement_plane: receiver-side output during fault isolation
measurements.boundary: temporary degraded output while the faulty leg is isolated; not a steady degraded service level

measurements.name: fault_isolation_transient_duration
measurements.measurement_plane: fault transient and isolation interval
measurements.boundary: temporary reduced-output period before recovery
conditions: single-leg fault isolation and standby-leg reassignment

measurements.name: post_fault_recovered_output_power
measurements.measurement_plane: receiver-side output after healthy inverter-leg reassignment
measurements.boundary: recovered degraded-mode output; not nominal full-power service
conditions: article reports recovery within less than 50 ms

measurements.name: experimental_fault_recovery_time
measurements.measurement_plane: fault detection, relay actuation and output stabilization sequence
measurements.boundary: reported total recovery time; article breaks it into approximately 5 ms processing, 35–40 ms relay actuation and 5 ms stabilization

measurements.name: simulated_fault_detection_latency
measurements.measurement_plane: MATLAB/FPGA control model fault detection result
measurements.boundary: simulation output; distinct from experimentally measured total recovery
conditions: fault detection from inverter current/voltage deviations

measurements.name: degraded_operation_efficiency
measurements.measurement_plane: system efficiency as reported during degraded operation
measurements.boundary: paper-reported efficiency; exact meter planes, fault mix and uncertainty are not specified in the public text extraction

measurements.name: resonant_operating_frequency
measurements.measurement_plane: transmitter compensation/resonant operating frequency
measurements.boundary: design operating frequency, not a measured energy-transfer result

known_unknowns: The article excludes misalignment effects from its analysis; the record is not a geometry/misalignment qualification.
The 1000 W design target and 800 W nominal experimental output are distinct reported quantities and must not be reconciled into a single rating.

The public article text describes different leg/coil configurations in different sections (three-leg/two-coil simulation, six-legged hardware inverter and four legs energizing coils); exact prototype topology must be resolved before matched hardware replication.
Exact source-side and receiver-side meter planes, meter calibration, uncertainty budget and energy-balance residual are not fully stated in the abstract/summary text.
Simulation-based 30–45 ms fault detection is kept separate from the approximately 50 ms experimental fault recovery report.
The laboratory prototype is not a public-roadway pilot, and no all-weather availability or fleet-scale utilization is established.

The article reports both a 90–92% normal efficiency range and >88–90% degraded range without a fully resolved meter-boundary comparison; do not rank against the 50 kW IPT DC-to-DC prototype or the VINCI motorway pilot.

The stated 100-trial-style ML split/cross-validation settings do not by themselves establish zero false accepts, fault coverage or safety certification; raw independent fault datasets and confusion matrices require review.
